name: Turvel Passionfruit-Cardamom Calm
description: A lightly carbonated functional soft drink marketed for stress reduction, combining synth-passionfruit and cardamom with a licensed anxiolytic compound approved for over-the-counter use. Part of Omnicorp's wellness beverage line.
flavor_profile: Soft, approachable passionfruit sweetness with warm cardamom spice; very low carbonation for a 'calm' mouthfeel; a faint floral bitterness on the back palate from the anxiolytic compound; pleasant but unremarkable
cultural_context: Turvel Calm is the drink of quiet desperation — bought by Tier 2 workers managing anxiety without access to proper healthcare, and by Tier 3 professionals self-medicating through brutal work cycles; the anxiolytic compound is mild but real, and regulars build a subtle tolerance that keeps them buying.
story_hooks: An internal Omnicorp document leaked to the mesh suggests Turvel Calm's anxiolytic dosage was deliberately set just below dependency threshold — close enough to build habitual purchasing, far enough to avoid regulation.

A Tier 2 community organizer is distributing Turvel Calm at political meetings — not for the taste, but because the anxiolytic compound subtly suppresses the neurological markers that corponation surveillance systems flag as 'agitation risk'.

The chemist who developed Turvel Calm's formula is trying to blow the whistle on a planned formula change that would cross the dependency threshold — she needs help getting her evidence out before Omnicorp finds her.
